title: MYC_V1-Related Genes Affect Gastric Cancer Proliferation by Regulating Energy Metabolism and Analysis of Therapeutic Targets.
authors: Xu, Duo; Peng, Lingyi; He, Jing; Wang, Xue; Xia, Jiaqi
one_liner_zh: 该文基于MYC_V1相关基因构建胃癌预后模型并筛选药物靶点，虽涉及分子对接但核心是肿瘤预后与代谢，非蛋白质-DNA互作或TF-DNA结合机制研究，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is the fifth leading cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Treatment options for advanced GC remain limited, owing to the frequent emergence of drug resistance. This highlights an urgent clinical need for novel therapeutic targets. Abnormal energy metabolism is a hallmark feature of cancer. MYC_V1-driven metabolic reprogramming plays a pivotal role in tumor progression. However, the specific mechanisms by which MYC_V1-related genes regulate energy metabolism in GC remains poorly understood. We employed single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA) to evaluate multiple tumor hallmarks in GC. A prognostic risk model was constructed based on MYC_V1-related genes, with the risk score (RS) used to stratify patients into distinct risk groups. A nomogram was developed and validated using calibration curves. Through the systematic molecular docking screening of 8327 compounds, potential therapeutic agents were identified. Functional experiments, including the CCK-8 assay, wound-healing assay and ATP production assay, were conducted to validate the role of NDUFV2 in GC progression. This study identified MYC_V1 as the primary risk factor affecting the overall survival (OS) in GC patients (p = 0.038). A prognostic risk model was successfully constructed based on eight MYC_V1-related genes (KPNA2, MCM2, MCM4, NDUFV2, PDK4, MPO, IGFBP1, and STC2). The RS was confirmed as an independent prognostic factor. The prognostic risk model accurately predicted patient 1-, 3-, and 5-year OS in GC patients. Tumor microenvironment analysis revealed significant differences in immune cell infiltration patterns between high-risk and low-risk groups. High-throughput drug screening and molecular docking identified camptothecin (CPT) and vinblastine as showing strong therapeutic potential for high-risk patients. Experimental validation demonstrated that NDUFV2 was significantly overexpressed in GC tissues, and its knockdown markedly suppressed the proliferation, migration capacity, and intracellular ATP production in GC cells, confirming the critical role of NDUFV2 in GC progression. These findings establish NDUFV2 as a potential therapeutic target in GC.
abstract_zh: 胃癌（GC）是全球癌症相关死亡率的第五大原因。由于频繁出现的耐药性，晚期GC的治疗选择仍然有限。这凸显了对新型治疗靶点的迫切临床需求。异常能量代谢是癌症的一个标志性特征。MYC_V1驱动的代谢重编程在肿瘤进展中发挥关键作用。然而，MYC_V1相关基因调控GC能量代谢的具体机制仍知之甚少。我们采用单样本基因集富集分析（ssGSEA）评估GC中的多种肿瘤标志。基于MYC_V1相关基因构建了一个预后风险模型，并使用风险评分（RS）将患者分为不同风险组。开发了一个列线图，并通过校准曲线进行验证。通过对8327种化合物进行系统性分子对接筛选，识别出潜在治疗药物。功能实验，包括CCK-8实验、伤口愈合实验和ATP生成实验，用于验证NDUFV2在GC进展中的作用。本研究将MYC_V1确定为影响GC患者总生存期（OS）的主要风险因素（p = 0.038）。基于八个MYC_V1相关基因（KPNA2、MCM2、MCM4、NDUFV2、PDK4、MPO、IGFBP1和STC2）成功构建了一个预后风险模型。RS被确认为独立预后因素。该预后风险模型准确预测了GC患者的1年、3年和5年OS。肿瘤微环境分析显示，高风险组和低风险组之间的免疫细胞浸润模式存在显著差异。高通量药物筛选和分子对接识别出喜树碱（CPT）和长春碱对高风险患者显示出强治疗潜力。实验验证表明，NDUFV2在GC组织中显著过表达，其敲低显著抑制了GC细胞的增殖、迁移能力和细胞内ATP生成，确认了NDUFV2在GC进展中的关键作用。这些发现将NDUFV2确立为GC中的潜在治疗靶点。
